rules.title: Limit on charges before start of tenancy (no application fees by lessors)
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a landlord may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit, and a lock-change fee. Application, pet, cleaning, amenity and all other upfront charges by the lessor are forbidden.
rules.key_value: Only first month's rent, last month's rent, security deposit, lock-change fee
rules.coverage_conditions: All lessors of residential rental property in Massachusetts, at or before the start of a tenancy.
rules.exemptions: Licensed real estate brokers acting as a separate bona fide business may charge fees under 254 CMR 7.00, according to the article.
rules.penalty: Tenants have recovered treble damages and attorney's fees for unlawful application fees (Perry v. Equity Residential Management, D. Mass. 2014).
rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks ( MGL Ch 186 Section 15B ).
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source (landlord trade association blog). It gives the effective date only as 'since the 1970s'. The article advises that requiring applicants to pay third-party screening services is legally risky, but there is no case law on that point.

rules.title: Licensed broker fee disclosure requirements for prospective tenants
rules.requirement: Only licensed brokers or salespersons may charge prospective tenants a fee for finding housing. At the first personal meeting, the broker must give a written notice stating the fee amount, the time and manner of payment, and whether the fee depends on a lease being signed. The applicant signs the notice, or the broker records the refusal.
rules.coverage_conditions: Licensed real estate brokers and salespersons who find rental housing for prospective tenants for a fee.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only when a licensed broker is involved in the transaction.

rules.quoted_span: In addition to holding a valid license, the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement.
rules.conflict_note: This is an archived secondary article with no effective date given. Later Massachusetts legislation on who pays broker fees may have changed tenant-paid broker fees; this document does not reflect any such change, so verify current law.
